findings.issue: For ref.kind in {registry, application}, fetchRecordForExplain returns a non-null sentinel and resolveFor calls getRecord unconditionally (it does NOT guard by kind), emitting record_fetch ok:true -- a vacuous step for non-record refs, not labelled N/A. Verdict parity is preserved (no deny->allow flip, no oracle leak), so this is a nit. However the docstring at line 27 ('resolveFor nikogda ne vyzovet getRecord dlya etih vidov') is factually wrong: the resolver DOES call getRecord for every ref kind; the sentinel is exactly what prevents a spurious not_found.
findings.suggestion: Either label the step record_fetch ok:true note:'n/a for non-record ref', or correct the line-27 comment to state the sentinel-not-a-lie rationale accurately (resolver always calls getRecord; sentinel keeps the step honest).

findings.issue: The endpoint-level parity property test asserts the endpoint verdict against a hardcoded expectedVerdict constant across read/create/update/delete x allow/no_grant/not_found, not against a live resolveFor baseline run on the same deps. It validates endpoint behaviour, not a true differential parity (endpoint == production resolveFor). Acceptable for a nit; closes the iter-1 R-5 gap structurally.
findings.suggestion: Optionally run resolveFor directly on the equivalent deps and assert endpoint verdict === baseline verdict, instead of comparing to a constant.

ff_rc5_verdict.rationale: role-criticality-isolation.sh (owned by T-0040) diffs merge-base(dev,HEAD)..HEAD against a frozen-foundation set that includes grant-resolver.ts. T-0136 BUILD (be07613) edits the resolver (76+/4-, trace-mode param + 9 trace points) -> red on branch. This is NOT a real prohibition: (1) the excludes file covers only migrations, not frozen-core, so a legitimate resolver edit cannot be band-excluded by design -- the freeze means 'no drift since dev base', not 'never edited'; (2) grant-resolver.ts was legitimately edited on dev many times AFTER T-0040 (T-0035, T-0118, T-0032, T-0034, T-0033, T-0021) -- each red-on-branch, green-post-merge; (3) the base is dynamic, so once T-0136 merges into dev the resolver edit lands on dev and merge-base for any future branch includes it -> grant-resolver.ts falls out of the diff -> FF-RC5 greens (same path as T-0143); (4) grant-resolver-isolation.sh (FF-R6, the authoritative owner-freeze for the resolver module) PASSES -- frozen NEIGHBORS object-handle/grant-lattice/types untouched, no second authority, ports not bypassed. The substantive guard for the resolver edit is Axis 1 (byte-identical behaviour when traceOut===undefined), confirmed in iter-1 and not regressed (resolver outside the fix-commit diff).

role_gap_evidence: FF-RC5 (T-0040 role-criticality-isolation.sh) lists grant-resolver.ts as a byte-frozen foundation file, yet the resolver is the legitimately-evolving PDP core (FF-R6 owns its real freeze). The two checks disagree on whether grant-resolver.ts is editable; FF-RC5 produces a guaranteed red-on-branch for every reviewed resolver BUILD (>=6 historical) that only greens post-merge. Candidate evidence for either (a) a frozen-core excludes mechanism analogous to the migration excludes, or (b) demoting grant-resolver.ts out of FF-RC5's frozen set since FF-R6 already governs it -- to stop a permanent false-red on the merge gate.

Endpoint-level verdict parity is still asserted against a hardcoded constant, not a live resolveFor baseline (R-5-resid). A fitness check proving explain.verdict == production-PDP.verdict (differential, not constant-compare) would convert the central AC-1 claim from 'tested by example' to 'provably equal'.
